findings: The fifth nominal test calls the C12 consumer only after real typed-operation controls, persisted choice, preview and a separate financial approval have succeeded. Missing controls are a failing expectation, not an accepted absence or skip.
The approval helper requires the pending approval stage and the exact proposed amount. A draft PR of 100 cannot count as approval of the selected 140; approval after Apply is not substituted.
The no-operation choice records financialApproval=false and keeps preparation disabled. This is a safe UI assertion and does not claim positive Apply coverage.
The public C12 HTTP receipt mapping really exposes receiptId, surface, version and outcome; the helper's applied-receipt assertion matches that mapping.

Response loss intercepts the original completed HTTP handler response, with no synthetic fulfill, route.fetch, direct test mutation or automatic mutation retry. It does not independently prove the domain-commit to case-reconciliation interruption window.
A fresh page and admission are not labeled a native process restart. Pending financial categories retain null complete totals.
